record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Discrete Geometry and Optimization
record.context_brief: Rigidity meaning of Schatten dual variables
record.original_question: For the non-convex Schatten p-quasi-norm regularization approach to fixed-dimensional localization, what rigidity-theoretic meaning does the dual vector y in the first-order critical point conditions have? More specifically, do rigidity-theoretic results that interpret semidefinite-programming dual variables as edge stresses satisfying equilibrium conditions have counterparts in the Schatten quasi-norm regularization setting?

evidence.quote: Along the same direction, it will be interesting to study the rigidity-theoretic implications of Schatten quasi-norm regularization. A starting point could be to understand the rigidity-theoretic interpretations of the dual vector y in the definition of the first-order critical point.

So and Ye state that each dual variable in the SDP relaxation corresponds to a stress on an edge of the input graph, and the optimality conditions correspond to a certain equilibrium condition on the input graph. A natural question would be whether these results have counterparts in the Schatten quasi-norm regularization setting.

artifact.category_tag: graph rigidity and sensor network localization
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the fixed-dimensional sensor network localization problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$: given a graph $G=(V,E)$, a subset $V_a\subseteq V$ of anchor nodes with known positions $a_i\in\mathbb{R}^d$ ($i\in V_a$), and measured squared distances $d_{ij}^2$ for each edge $(i,j)\in E$, one seeks positions $x_i\in\mathbb{R}^d$ ($i\in V\setminus V_a$) consistent with the measurements. A standard semidefinite-programming (SDP) relaxation lifts the problem to recovering a Gram matrix $Y\in\mathbb{S}^n_+$ satisfying linear constraints $\langle A_{ij},Y\rangle = d_{ij}^2$. It is known that for the SDP relaxation each dual variable $y_{ij}$ associated with edge $(i,j)$ may be interpreted as a stress on that edge, and the optimality (KKT) conditions become a stress equilibrium condition on the framework $(G,p)$.

Now consider, instead of the SDP relaxation, a non-convex Schatten $p$-quasi-norm regularized formulation (with $0<p<1$) of the form
$$\min_{Y\succeq 0}\ \|Y\|_{S_p}^p \ \ \text{subject to}\ \ \langle A_{ij},Y\rangle = d_{ij}^2,\ (i,j)\in E,$$
where $\|Y\|_{S_p}^p=\sum_k \sigma_k(Y)^p$ is the Schatten $p$-quasi-norm raised to the $p$-th power. Let $y=(y_{ij})_{(i,j)\in E}$ be the vector of Lagrange/dual multipliers appearing in the first-order critical point (KKT) conditions of this Schatten quasi-norm regularized problem.

Question: Provide a rigidity-theoretic interpretation of the dual vector $y$ for the Schatten $p$-quasi-norm regularized localization problem. In particular, determine whether each component $y_{ij}$ can be interpreted as a (possibly generalized) edge stress on the framework $(G,p)$, and whether the first-order critical point conditions correspond to a (possibly modified) equilibrium condition on $G$, analogous to the SDP case.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work establishing a rigidity-theoretic interpretation (edge stresses, equilibrium) for dual variables of the non-convex Schatten p-quasi-norm regularized sensor network localization problem. Related literature characterizes duality mappings for Schatten norms and studies Schatten-p quasi-norm regularization for low-rank recovery, but no counterpart to the SDP stress/equilibrium interpretation appears to have been derived. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A novel variational form of the Schatten-p quasi-norm
status_evidence.snippet: Variational forms of the Schatten-p quasi-norm are defined for continuous values of p ∈ (0, 1).
status_evidence.claim: Schatten-p quasi-norm regularization is studied for low-rank recovery, but without rigidity-theoretic dual interpretation.

status_evidence.title: Duality Mapping for Schatten Matrix Norms
status_evidence.snippet: The duality mapping over the space of matrices equipped with Schatten norms has been fully characterized.
status_evidence.claim: Duality for Schatten norms is characterized abstractly, not in terms of framework stresses/equilibrium.
